title: Fennel, Orange and Olive Salad
subtitle: Thinly shaved fennel with orange segments and kalamata olives
excerpt: Very thinly shaved fennel with peeled orange segments, kalamata olives and fresh mint, dressed in olive oil and lemon juice. A Sicilian-inspired winter salad with clean, bright flavours.
sourceNotes: Fennel and orange salad is a classic of Sicilian and southern Italian cooking (insalata di finocchio e arancia), associated with the island's abundance of both citrus fruits and fennel. It appears in Elizabeth David's Italian Food (1954) and has since become widely adopted in British and American cooking as an elegant winter salad that needs no cooking. The addition of olives follows the Sicilian tradition.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shave the fennel up to an hour ahead and keep in iced water to stay crisp. Assemble just before serving.

content.text: Fennel and orange salad depends on paper-thin fennel. Thick slices are tough and overwhelmingly anise in flavour; thin shavings are delicate and the anise becomes a background note. Use a mandoline if you have one, or a very sharp knife and patience. The orange should be segmented so there is no pith or membrane.

items.prepNote: outer layers removed, very thinly shaved, fronds reserved
from the fennel above, roughly chopped

content.text: Whisk together {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, the juice of {{lemon}} lemon, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Arrange the shaved fennel on a large plate. Add the orange segments and kalamata olives. Scatter over the mint and fennel fronds if using. Drizzle the dressing over. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Fennel is too thick and tough
items.cause: Sliced with a knife rather than a mandoline, or sliced too thick.
items.fix: Use a mandoline set to 2 mm or less. Alternatively, halve the fennel bulb, place cut-side down on the board and use a very sharp chef's knife with short, controlled strokes.

items.cause: Fennel is at its bitterest raw and in thick pieces.
items.fix: Shave very thinly. Submerge the shaved fennel in iced water for 10 minutes, then drain and dry; this removes some bitterness.

content.text: Fennel and orange salad is a Sicilian winter classic, served on the island when both fennel and blood oranges are in season from December to March. Elizabeth David introduced it to British cooks in the 1950s; it has since become one of the most recommended winter salads in British food writing. It is excellent alongside oily fish such as grilled mackerel or smoked salmon, or as a refreshing contrast to rich braised meat.
